clips.text: One traffic jam stretched a hundred kilometres — and lasted twelve days.
You are sitting in it. The brake lights ahead have not moved since sunrise.
A hundred kilometres of cars, standing still for twelve days — moving about a kilometre a day.
And here is the strangest part. The jam is moving — backwards, toward you.
You do not drive out of it. It drives past you.
So why does a traffic jam last twelve days when there's no crash, no closure, nothing blocking the road?
The jam is a wave travelling backwards — and inside your car, the fuel and the water are running out. Tap the video link under my name.
